papers.abstract: Direct photolithography offers a transformative photoresist-free route for high-precision integration in electronic and optoelectronic platforms. Despite significant advancements in quantum dots (QDs), existing methods often degrade optoelectronic performance due to the inherent surface ligand changes during photolithographic processing. Here, we introduce a reversible photolithography strategy to overcome this bottleneck. This strategy is based on the first wavelength-gated, reversible ligand crosslinking and decrosslinking cycle, enabling the dynamic and reversible control over the photolithographic process. Using this approach, we achieve high-efficient and high-fidelity QD photolithography with restored QD structure and functionality. The reversible process further enables high-performance electroluminescence, with one of the highest luminance values of 125,016 cd m-2 at 5.0 V and a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.41%. Moreover, we demonstrate an ultrahigh-resolution nano-pixelated device with a peak EQE of 17.08% at 21,000 PPI. This work presents a photo-reversible crosslinking system that decouples photolithographic patterning from performance degradation, offering a versatile platform for high-end QD-based displays and other advanced optoelectronics.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most aggressive malignancies and is characterized by a high degree of heterogeneity. However, HCC treatment remains difficult, highlighting the need to better define molecular subgroups of HCC and understand their potential relationships with therapeutic response. Methods In this study, we established 20 patient‐derived organoids and 12 patient‐derived cell lines from 20 individuals diagnosed with HCC. These models were comprehensively characterized using whole‐exome sequencing, RNA sequencing, drug screening, and hepatitis B virus (HBV)‐targeting PCR with a focus on HBV‐related HCC. Results Based on transcriptomic profiling, this study classified HCC into two molecular subtypes, aligning with previously reported classifications. Drug screening revealed that the greater enrichment of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling pathway was associated with increased sensitivity to everolimus and lenvatinib. Integrated transcriptomic and drug‐response analyses further identified candidate genes associated with lenvatinib response. In addition, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis targeting the HBV surface, core, and X genes demonstrated noticeable discrepancies relative to the clinically reported HBV infection status. Notably, HBV DNA detection was associated with activation of the calcium signalling pathway and oxaliplatin response. Conclusions This study provides a valuable resource for investigating the biology and pharmacological characteristics of HCC, particularly in the context of molecular subtypes and HBV‐associated mechanisms. Ultimately, these findings offer additional insights into HCC heterogeneity and drug response and may serve as a basis for further investigation of molecular determinants of therapeutic response.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Histological subtype and resection completeness are established prognostic factors in retroperitoneal liposarcoma, but evidence often derives from resected primary disease. We characterized management and post-referral survival in a referral cohort. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 61 patients managed from May 2015 to September 2025. Overall survival (OS) was measured from first presentation at our center. Kaplan–Meier and exploratory Cox analyses were performed, allowing the association between tumor diameter and mortality to vary over time. Results: Forty-two patients had primary disease, and 19 had recurrent disease; 12 had well-differentiated liposarcoma (WDLPS), and 49 had dedifferentiated liposarcoma (DDLPS). Among 24 patients who underwent surgery, 21 had macroscopically complete (R0/R1) resection. Twenty-five patients died. No deaths occurred in WDLPS; median OS was 29.8 months in DDLPS (p = 0.008). In DDLPS, recurrent versus primary disease was not associated with OS (hazard ratio [HR], 0.99; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.41–2.38). Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status ≥ 2 (n = 6 in the entire cohort) was associated with poorer OS (adjusted HR, 8.03; 95% CI, 2.20–29.36), and the association between tumor diameter and mortality varied over time (adjusted interaction HR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.07–1.95). Conclusions: Observed post-referral survival differed by histological subtype. Among patients with DDLPS, no survival difference between primary and recurrent disease was demonstrated, but the wide CI and referral-related survivor selection preclude an inference of equivalence. Associations involving performance status and time-varying tumor diameter were exploratory and require external validation.

papers.abstract: Lorlatinib is a third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK)/ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) that has been shown to have high efficacy in the first line setting for treatment of advanced ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, some adverse events have been described that require proper follow-up and management to obtain the maximum benefit from treatment and minimize risk to the patient. These include dyslipidemia and weight gain, conditions that in Latin America have a high prevalence in the general population, which coupled with limitations in timely access to specialized care, could influence both manifestation and management. The objective of this consensus is to provide recommendations tailored to our real-world setting that will optimize the monitoring and early management of toxicities in patients treated with lorlatinib in Latin America.

papers.abstract: Background Zoledronic acid is used to prevent skeletal complications in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and bone metastases. Real world data on its use in resource-limited setting, particularly in sub-saharan Africa, remain scarce. Aim To describe clinical outcomes, skeletal-related events, safety and quality of life in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) and bone metastases treated with zoledronic acid in Côte d’Ivoire. Methods We conducted a retrospective, single center cohort study including 144 patients with mCRPC and bone metastases treated with zoledronic acid at Treichville university Hospital between January 2019 and December 2021. The primary endpoint was skeletal event-free survival (SEFS) defined as the time from the first zoledronic acid administration to the first on-treatment skeletal related event (SRE). Patients without an SRE were censored at their last available follow-up. Results The median age was 67 years (range: 42–91), and 133 patients (92.4%) were older than 50 years. Before zoledronic acid initiation, 59 patients (41.0%) had experienced at least one skeletal-related event. After treatment initiation, 30 patients (20.8%) experienced at least one new on-treatment SRE, whereas 114 (79.2%) did not. Among patients who experienced an SRE, the median time to the first event was 9 months (range 5-11). Median SEFS was not reached and the estimated 12-month SEFS was 79.2%. The most frequently documented adverse events were bone pain (18.8%), constipation (18.1%) and nausea (9.7%). FACT-G data at both baseline and 12-month were available for 129 patients (89.6%) and mean scores across all four FACT-G domains, as well as the total FACT-G score, were numerically lower at 12 months than at baseline. Conclusion In this retrospective cohort of patients with mCRPC and bone metastases, 20.8% experienced a new SRE after zoledronic acid initiation, while median SEFS was not reached. FACT-G scores decreased during follow-up. These findings provide real-world data on zoledronic acid use in a resource-limited setting.

papers.abstract: Objective Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a leading cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Conventional biomarkers alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and des-gamma-carboxy prothrombin (DCP) have diagnostic limitations, particularly for early-stage disease. This study investigated the expression profile of ORC1 in HBV-related liver disease and its association with HBV infection, disease progression, and prognosis. Methods 178 participants were recruited: 124 HBV-positive cases (49 HBV-HCC, 33 HBV-cirrhosis, 42 chronic hepatitis B) and 54 HBV-negative controls (35 non-HBV-HCC, 19 hepatic hemangioma). Tissue ORC1 was detected by immunohistochemistry, and serum ORC1 was measured by ELISA in a subset of 17 HBV-HCC patients with available serum. Logistic regression identified factors associated with high ORC1 expression. ROC curves were used to evaluate the discrimination of tissue ORC1, AFP, and DCP for HBV-HCC, and the correlation between ORC1 and tumor diameter was analyzed. TCGA-LIHC data were used for external validation. Results Tissue ORC1 was significantly upregulated in HBV-positive patients, and HBV infection was independently associated with high ORC1 expression (P<0. 001). ORC1 expression increased progressively from chronic hepatitis B to cirrhosis to HCC. In a subset of 17 HBV-HCC patients with available serum, tissue and serum ORC1 were moderately correlated (Spearman rs=0. 554, 95% CI 0. 085–0. 822, P = 0. 021). Tissue ORC1 showed moderate discrimination between HBV-HCC and HBV-LC (AUC = 0. 64) and between HBV-HCC and CHB (AUC = 0. 66). ORC1 expression was not significantly associated with tumor diameter ( P >0. 05). High ORC1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival in TCGA-LIHC (HR = 1. 7, P = 0. 0026). Conclusion ORC1 upregulation is independently associated with HBV infection and increases with disease progression in HBV-related liver disease. Although tissue ORC1 showed only moderate discrimination for HBV-HCC, high ORC1 expression was associated with poorer overall survival in TCGA-LIHC. These findings suggest that ORC1 is primarily a proliferation- and progression-related marker in HBV-related liver disease.

papers.abstract: Background BI-RADS category 4 breast lesions are suspicious and generally undergo tissue diagnosis, but malignancy risk remains heterogeneous across BI-RADS 4A, 4B, and 4C. We developed and internally validated an interpretable mammography-based model for risk stratification within this diagnostic category. Methods This single-center retrospective diagnostic prediction study included 441 patients, each contributing one index BI-RADS 4 mammographic lesion. Outcomes were verified histopathologically in 397 lesions and by longitudinal imaging stability in 44. Three primary models and a sensitivity model excluding BI-RADS were evaluated. Internal validation used 1,000 paired patient-level bootstrap resamples in which imputation, encoding, standardization, penalty selection, LASSO selection, and coefficient estimation were repeated. Results Of 441 lesions, 165 were malignant. Malignancy rates were 15.7% (34/216), 46.4% (70/151), and 82.4% (61/74) in BI-RADS 4A, 4B, and 4C, respectively. The final model retained BI-RADS 4B, BI-RADS 4C, architectural distortion, circularity-deficit irregularity score, contour serration score, and normalized GLCM contrast. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.770 (95% CI, 0.729-0.815) for BI-RADS only, 0.774 (0.733-0.814) for clinical plus BI-RADS, and 0.841 (0.809-0.877) for the full mammography-based model. Clinical variables did not improve validated performance. The full model improved corrected AUC versus BI-RADS only by 0.072 (0.028-0.108) and versus clinical plus BI-RADS by 0.067 (0.029-0.103). Its corrected calibration intercept was 0.002 (-0.209 to 0.208) and slope was 1.445 (1.140-1.753). Within-category AUCs were 0.785, 0.721, and 0.758 for BI-RADS 4A, 4B, and 4C; the pathology-only corrected AUC was 0.835 (0.799-0.871). Conclusion Structured and quantitative mammographic features improved internally validated discrimination and within-category risk stratification beyond BI-RADS subcategory alone. Because predicted risks were under-dispersed and validation was limited to one center, the model should be used only as a research-stage risk-stratification and prioritization tool, not to replace biopsy. External validation and recalibration are required before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Previous studies of ABO blood group and breast cancer prognosis have yielded inconsistent results, mainly evaluating blood group itself as a prognostic factor. We investigated whether the prognostic associations of clinicopathological factors differ according to ABO blood group in stage II–III breast cancer. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 1540 patients with stage II–III breast cancer who underwent curative resection between 2010 and 2019. Blood group-specific prognostic analyses of breast cancer-specific survival (BCSS) were performed, with continuous variables analyzed without dichotomization. Based on the observed patterns, an exploratory interaction between blood group B and pathological nodal status was tested, and its robustness was assessed using a permutation test and sensitivity analyses. Results: ABO blood group was not associated with BCSS overall (p = 0.641). In blood group-stratified multivariable analyses, ≥4 lymph node metastases was an independent adverse prognostic factor in blood groups A, O, and AB, but not in blood group B. A significant interaction was observed between blood group B and pathological nodal status (0–3 vs. ≥4 nodes) (p for interaction < 0.001; permutation-adjusted p = 0.004). Among patients with 0–3 lymph node metastases, blood group B was independently associated with worse BCSS (hazard ratio, 2.04; 95% confidence interval, 1.25–3.32; p = 0.004), consistently across sensitivity analyses; this association was more evident among patients who received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. In this subgroup, blood group B was also associated with more distant and visceral recurrence (all p < 0.05). Conclusions: The prognostic association of nodal burden in stage II–III breast cancer may differ according to ABO blood group. The exploratory findings in patients with limited nodal involvement suggest that blood group B may identify a subgroup characterized by worse BCSS and increased distant and visceral recurrence. Given the small number of events in blood group B with ≥4 nodes and possible differences according to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant independent validation.

papers.abstract: Transformed small cell lung cancer (T-SCLC) is most commonly observed in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma and represents an important mechanism of acquired resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs). Its reported clinical incidence is approximately 3%-10%. Patients with T-SCLC often experience rapid disease progression and poor overall prognosis, and no established standard treatment regimen is currently available. We report a case of advanced EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma with RB1 , TP53 , and BRCA2 co-mutations that underwent small-cell transformation during treatment. Small-cell transformation was detected through close surveillance and confirmed by repeat biopsy. The patient subsequently received individualized multimodal therapy, including chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and local radiotherapy, and remained alive 43 months after the initial diagnosis.

papers.abstract: Antigen-presenting cancer-associated fibroblasts (apCAFs), commonly defined by MHC class II molecules, CD74, and related transcriptional programs, exhibit divergent functions across gastrointestinal tumors. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, mesothelium-derived apCAFs promote regulatory T-cell differentiation and suppress effector responses, whereas their abundance in gastric cancer is associated with earlier-stage disease, longer survival, and improved immunotherapy responses. This paradox may reflect microenvironmental context and classifications that conflate transcriptional state, cellular origin, and immune function. apCAFs may therefore represent reversible, context-dependent states defined by origin, MHC class II-restricted antigen presentation, and co-stimulatory capacity. We propose a two-layer model that has not been validated in apCAFs. In this model, the chromatin accessibility of CIITA, CD40, CD80, and CD86 constructs a functional licensing range, while interferon - γ (IFN - γ), interleukin-1 (IL-1), and transforming growth factor - β (TGF - β) guide the formation of specific phenotypes within this range. Insufficient co-stimulation may favor immune tolerance; activation of co-stimulatory programs may support CD4 + T-cell help and CD8 + T-cell infiltration. Treatment-induced changes in CAF composition may reflect selective survival or genuine state transitions. Distinguishing these mechanisms requires lineage tracing, longitudinal single-cell transcriptomic and chromatin profiling, and patient-derived organoid–fibroblast co-cultures. Neoadjuvant therapy and serial endoscopic sampling provide feasible settings for capturing transient states. This framework supports replacing broad CAF depletion with temporally and state-informed functional reprogramming.

papers.abstract: Effective prophylactic interventions for exercise-induced joint damage and preclinical osteoarthritis remain elusive, as abnormal mechanical loading drives pathology through a dual pyroptotic loop between chondrocytes and macrophages. We present PMUC, a mechano-responsive lubricating hydrogel engineered for graded joint protection and repair. Mimicking native lubrication, intra-articular PMUC forms a persistent hydration layer that dissipates mechanical stress. Under pathological load, stress-induced reactive oxygen species trigger mannose and nanocomplex release. This cascade activates the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway, suppressing Caspase-3/GSDME-mediated chondrocyte pyroptosis while concurrently reprogramming macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles. Enriched with XIAP and OTULIN proteins, these in situ-generated extracellular vesicles act as intercellular messengers that disrupt the inflammatory cycle and facilitate matrix regeneration. In preclinical rat models of high-load exercise and post-traumatic OA, PMUC prevents cartilage erosion and achieves full regeneration with restored locomotion within eight weeks. Here we show that PMUC integrates adaptive lubrication with stress-triggered immune-metabolic modulation, offering a first‑in‑class strategy to protect joints and alleviate early OA.

papers.abstract: This work investigates the energy required to manipulate a memory bit using a superconducting vortex confined in a nanoscale double-well pinning potential. In the experiments, various double-well systems subjected to sinusoidal forces is explored, and the effects of both driving force and frequency is analyzed. Results reveal characteristic stochastic resonance behavior for weak drives and adiabatic manipulation at strong, low-frequency drives. Although our experimental method requires a steady sinusoidal drive incompatible with Landauer's erasure protocol, our numerical analysis demonstrates that the work required for such bit manipulation (erasure) is within an order of magnitude of Landauer's limit ( k B T ln 2 ) at 4.2 K. These findings open possibilities for creating highly efficient memory elements that could be integrated with cryogenic quantum circuits or function as topological quantum computing qubits; thereby contributing to memory devices with lower energy consumption and mitigating the escalating global energy demand in the computing industry.

papers.abstract: Development of long-read RNA sequencing technologies has paved the way to the exploration of RNA isoform diversity and its relevance in regulating cell fate. However, identifying new functional isoforms is still very difficult. Here, we leverage long-read RNA sequencing to study changes in isoforms during somatic cell reprogramming and identify novel isoforms occurring throughout cell state transitions. We demonstrate tight regulation of non-coding isoforms and show that isoform switching plays previously overlooked functional roles and outcomes in gene regulation and cell fate changes. We uncover a novel long non-coding RNA, Snhg26, that undergoes isoform switching during reprogramming to enhance the conversion of differentiated cells towards the pluripotent state. Knock-down of Snhg26 in mouse and human pluripotency models reveals that it is important for pluripotency acquisition. Together, our study provides a resource to study full-length isoform usage during cell fate change. It also demonstrates the power of long-read sequencing to identify functionally relevant gene isoforms in the context of cell plasticity.

papers.abstract: Signal transmission across membranes is usually mediated by the permeation of molecular species. Here we show that atomically thin graphene crystals, although impermeable to any ions or molecules, can transmit interfacial electrical potentials across electrolyte junctions without significant disruption. In monolayer graphene, applying an electrical potential at one graphene-electrolyte interface induces a similar responsive potential at the opposite side, with the magnitude governed by ionic sizes. By increasing the number of graphene layers, the response decays and vanishes at ~ 5 layers. Theoretical analysis attributes these observations to graphene's tunable charge-carrier concentration combined with its extreme thinness. This capability of transmitting activation stimuli without mass transport may find its applications in artificial synapses and other neuromorphic junctions.

papers.abstract: Developing organic photodetectors (OPDs) that can detect in deep shortwave infrared (deep-SWIR) region (1.2-1.6 μm) is technologically important. Yet, the performance of the state-of-the-art deep-SWIR OPDs remains substantially limited. Herein, we report a selenium-integrated quinoidal small molecular acceptor, SeBz-4Cl, enabling highly sensitive deep-SWIR photodetection. Selenium incorporation enhances quinoidal character along the conjugated backbone of the molecules, thus expanding absorption approaching 1.5 μm. Moreover, SeBz-4Cl with strengthened intermolecular interactions led to an ideal film morphology, which reduced Urbach energy and favored charge dynamics. Under -1 V voltage bias, the SeBz-4Cl-based OPD achieved a low dark current density of 2.97 × 10-7 A cm-2 and an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 7.8% at 1310 nm, together with a high specific detectivity (D*) exceeding 1011 Jones across 500-1400 nm, representing advanced deep-SWIR OPD performance. Furthermore, an optical communication system and a flexible imager under 1.2 μm illumination were demonstrated, highlighting potential of these deep-SWIR OPDs for information electronics and next generation optoelectronic applications in future.

papers.abstract: Solid oxide steam electrolysis offers the highest electrical efficiency for hydrogen production, yet wide-scale deployment remains constrained by durability. Here, we show that long-term stack durability can be strongly influenced by operating strategy, achieving 25,000 h of steam electrolysis operation in a full 70-cell solid oxide electrolysis cell stack under frequency-dependent electrochemical operation (AC:DC). This experiment represents, to our knowledge, the longest and lowest degradation operation reported for a full stack. The stack enters a stabilized regime with an average voltage degradation rate of 0.05 % kh⁻¹ (0.65 mV kh⁻¹ per cell) sustained for 22,000 h after initial conditioning. The behavior is evaluated against initial DC operation, prior full-stack benchmarks, impedance evolution, and post-test microstructural signatures. Periodic polarity inversion between electrolysis and fuel-cell modes modulates electrochemical polarization and heat generation, consistent with mitigating thermal and electrochemical gradients that develop during sustained DC electrolysis. Stack-level impedance evolution and post-mortem microstructural analysis demonstrate stabilization of electrochemical performance and suppression of degradation signatures commonly observed under DC operation, indicating that key degradation pathways are not activated under AC:DC operation. By shifting durability control from materials to operational strategy, AC:DC operation offers a scalable pathway toward long-lived solid oxide electrolysis for economically competitive green hydrogen production.

papers.abstract: Holography enables modulation of light waves to create three-dimensional (3D) displays with natural depth cues. Previous research on holographic displays primarily focused on synthesizing real images in free space while neglecting the physical display optics. Here, we propose an end-to-end, system-level design framework that accounts for the complete path from the illumination source to the retina by integrating optimized eyepiece optics. Joint optimization of the hologram, eyepiece optics, and component positions across polychromatic wavelengths and multiple depth channels corrects chromatic dispersion, optical aberrations, and geometric distortions while incorporating eyebox deployment, depth representation, and hologram bandwidth, enabling apochromatic and high-performance holographic displays. Two prototypes, a full-color, large depth-of-field (DOF), large field-of-view (FOV) holographic near-eye display and a full-color, large FOV, multi-focus 3D holographic freeform augmented-reality (AR) near-eye display, validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, providing valuable insights for advancing ergonomic holographic AR/virtual reality (VR) systems with realistic visual experiences.

papers.abstract: DNA polymerase ζ (Polζ) has emerged as a key reverse transcriptase in RNA-templated double-strand break repair (RT-DSBR), beyond its canonical role in translesion DNA synthesis (TLS). We present here the cryo-EM structure of yeast Polζ (including Rev1) in the act of reverse transcription, wherein the polymerase molds the replicative end of the bound RNA:DNA hybrid into B-like conformation and retains most contacts seen with DNA:DNA. Critically, the polymerase adopts the same conformation as with DNA:DNA, indicating its inherent versatility in accommodating both DNA:DNA and RNA:DNA substrates to preserve genome stability.

papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSC) exhibits substantial molecular and morphological heterogeneity, yet current morphology-based prognostic models often lack biological interpretability. We developed a transformer-based computational framework (CTransPath) to virtually predict gene expression directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide images. Morphology-associated genes were identified from the TCGA-HNSC cohort, and a 32-gene morphology-guided prognostic signature (MGP_HNSC32) based on H&E-derived predicted gene expression was developed using Random Survival Forest and multivariable Cox regression modeling. In TCGA-HNSC, the MGP_HNSC32 risk score significantly stratified patients by progression-free interval (PFI; HR = 4.13, 95% CI: 2.84-6.02), overall survival (OS; HR = 2.42, 95% CI: 1.78-3.29), and disease-specific survival (DSS; HR = 4.88, 95% CI: 2.95-8.06; all p < 0.001), and remained independently associated with prognosis after multivariable adjustment. High-risk tumors were enriched for cell cycle, E2F, MYC, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition pathways and displayed poorly differentiated histology with nuclear atypia and stromal desmoplasia. In contrast, low-risk tumors showed keratinizing morphology and immune-rich stroma, corresponding to differentiation- and metabolism-related transcriptional programs. In the independent HANCOCK cohort (n = 701), risk scores calculated entirely from H&E-derived predicted gene expression using the TCGA-derived coefficients and prespecified cutoff were associated with progression-free survival (HR = 1.40, 95% CI: 1.03-1.90, p = 0.034). However, the continuous risk score was not significantly associated with progression-free survival (HR = 1.001, 95% CI: 0.999-1.003, p = 0.328). MGP_HNSC32 links histomorphology to transcriptional programs and demonstrates preliminary prognostic associations using routine H&E images. The H&E-based gene-expression prediction component should be considered proof-of-concept, and further independent and prospective validation is required before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the anti-tumor effects of the natural flavonoid Isorhamnetin (ISO) on BC and elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms. We integrated network pharmacology and bioinformatic analysis to predict the core targets and pathways between BC and ISO. In vitro functional assays were performed using the human BC cell line 5637. Cell viability, proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, and adhesion were assessed via CCK-8, colony formation, flow cytometry, Transwell, and adhesion assays. Glycolytic function was evaluated by measuring extracellular acidification rate (ECAR), oxygen consumption rate (OCR), glucose uptake, and lactate production. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) were used to validate ISO-SRC binding. Western blot and RT-qPCR analyses were conducted to examine protein and mRNA expression of key signaling and glycolytic components. For the rescue experiments, SRC was overexpressed along with treatment using the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. ISO significantly inhibited BC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, adhesion, and glycolysis while inducing G0/G1 phase arrest and apoptosis. Network pharmacology and molecular docking identified SRC as a direct target of ISO, with CETSA confirming their binding. ISO treatment downregulated phosphorylation of SRC and its downstream effectors (PI3K, Akt, mTOR), reduced the expression of glycolytic enzymes (HK2, GLUT1, PFKFB3), and decreased ECAR, OCR, glucose uptake, and lactate production. SRC overexpression reversed the anti-tumor and anti-glycolytic effects of ISO. Furthermore, administration of LY294002 on this basis counteracted the effects induced by SRC overexpression, confirming the critical role of the SRC/PI3K/Akt axis. ISO inhibits the malignant progression of BC by directly targeting SRC to suppress glycolysis mediated by the PI3K/Akt signaling pathway. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for considering ISO as a potential metabolic-targeting agent for BC, warranting further preclinical evaluation.

Method development is limited by the lack of flexible simulation tools with known ground truth. Here, we present simPIC, a fast, memory-efficient framework for simulating realistic single-cell ATAC-seq count data across individuals and populations. simPIC models cell groups, batch effects, and genotype-dependent accessibility variation, enabling evaluation of population-scale methods, including chromatin accessibility quantitative trait locus mapping. Across multiple datasets and cell types, simPIC closely matches real data distributions while scaling to cohort sizes impractical for current tools.

papers.abstract: T-cell receptor (TCR) recognition of antigenic peptides presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules underpins adaptive immunity and T cell-based immunotherapy. However, the scarcity of complete interaction data and TCR cross-reactivity challenge robust prediction. Here, we present UpTCR, a unified progressive knowledge-transfer foundation model that learns from incomplete data to predict TCR-antigen-HLA binding. UpTCR progressively transfers knowledge from dimeric and trimeric interactions to tetrameric complexes and uses soft contrastive learning to mitigate false negatives. It outperforms existing methods in predicting TCR binding specificity and antigen-HLA binding affinity, particularly for neoantigens, and reveals pairwise residue-level interactions across the tetramer. UpTCR also transfers effectively to breast cancer cohorts with limited data. Prospective validation against melanoma antigen variants identifies eight immunogenic peptides that elicit T cell responses and one variant associated with immune escape. These findings establish UpTCR as a generalizable and interpretable tool for studying antigen recognition and advancing TCR-based immunotherapies.

papers.abstract: Social interaction requires the integration of information about self, other, and shared context. One of the proposed mechanisms supporting this coordination is interbrain synchrony - correlated neural activity between interacting individuals - yet its role in shaping social behavior remains unresolved. Here, we show that theta band synchrony in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) is closely linked to social interaction in mice and often precedes its onset. In male Shank2 mutant mice, a genetic model of social dysfunction, mPFC interbrain synchrony was diminished, along with a reduced population of mPFC neurons encoding multiple dimensions of social information. Optogenetic entrainment of theta synchrony was accompanied by increased interbrain coupling and social interaction in male Shank2-/- and Tbr1+/K228E mutant mice, two well-established genetic models of autism spectrum disorder (ASD). These findings identify prefrontal theta synchrony as a neural substrate that supports social behavior and provide a framework for understanding how coordinated neural activity across brains contributes to social interaction.

papers.abstract: Antibiotic resistance has become a critical public health problem, rendering many antibiotics ineffective. In particular, the evolution of extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) threatens β-lactams, the cornerstone of bacterial infection treatment. We investigated the evolution of Escherichia coli TEM-1 β-lactamase into ESBLs by constructing a combinatorially complete library of all 55,296 TEM-1 variants from 18 clinical mutations across 13 residues. We obtained over 9,000,000 fitness measurements under native (ampicillin) and non-native (aztreonam) selection. Graph-theoretic and epistatic analyses revealed that ampicillin selection produced weak epistasis and predictable evolutionary trajectories, whereas aztreonam selection induced extensive higher-order epistasis, increasing phenotypic unpredictability. Machine learning identified interpretable epistatic rules shaping these landscapes. Evolutionary statistics, including direct coupling analysis and latent generative landscapes, showed that top-performing ESBL variants followed conserved epistatic patterns observed in natural β-lactamases. Our integrated experimental-computational framework provides a foundation for predicting ESBL evolution and quantifying mutational contributions to ESBL variants.

papers.abstract: Intestinal epithelial integrity is essential for host defense, yet how epithelial junctional scaffolds coordinate antimicrobial immunity remains unclear. We show that the long GEF-H1 isoforms (mouse Arhgef2-207; human ARHGEF2-219) localize to adherens junctions in polarized epithelial cells through interactions with actin and Nectin-3, whereas the shorter Arhgef2-201 isoform localizes to tight junctions. Conditional deletion of epithelial Arhgef2-207 induces Arhgef2-201 expression, disrupts barrier integrity, activates autophagy, and causes small-intestinal inflammation. In human intestinal organoids, Listeria monocytogenes selectively depletes junction-associated ARHGEF2-219, triggering a switch to ARHGEF2-201 and RhoA- and STING-mediated autophagic signaling. This transition coincides with loss of the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase and epithelial polarity. Here we show that a pathogen-induced ARHGEF2 isoform switch links junctional perturbation to autophagic responses and immune activation, revealing a mechanism that couples barrier disruption to cell-intrinsic antimicrobial defense.

papers.abstract: Avian influenza poses a persistent pandemic threat, yet traditional vaccines face production delays. Self-amplifying mRNA (sa-mRNA) technology offers potential advantages, including rapid development, dose sparing, and enhanced, durable immunity. We evaluated ARCT-2304, a bicistronic sa-mRNA vaccine encoding H5N1 hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA), in a Phase 1 randomized, observer-blind trial (NCT06602531). Healthy adults (N = 212) received two doses of ARCT-2304 (1.5, 5, or 12 mcg) or control/placebo on a 4- or 8-week schedule. Primary outcomes evaluated safety and reactogenicity (solicited/unsolicited/serious adverse events [AEs]) and immunogenicity (HA inhibition and NA enzyme-linked lectin assays 28 days post-second dose). Immunogenicity results were benchmarked using serum from a prior study supporting licensure of an H5N1 vaccine. ARCT-2304 was well-tolerated, displaying mostly mild-to-moderate, transient, dose-dependent solicited AEs, with no safety concerns identified. Two doses elicited robust HA and NA humoral responses. An 8-week interval yielded higher magnitude and greater durability than a 4-week schedule, with neutralizing and anti-NA antibodies remaining significantly elevated 6-7 months post-second dose. ARCT-2304 also induced dose-dependent, Th1-polarized T-cell responses peaking at Day 29. These findings support advancing sa-mRNA platforms for pandemic influenza preparedness.

papers.abstract: Motion sickness (MS) is a common response to conflicting motion signals and can cause nausea, dizziness, malaise, and reduced activity. Sound can lessen MS, but how auditory cues influence the brain circuits that generate these symptoms is unclear. Here we show, using a repeated rotation paradigm in male mice, that a brief anticipatory tone reduces MS-like responses. We identify Cerebellin-2-expressing (Cbln2+) glutamatergic neurons in the medial vestibular nuclei (MVN), a brainstem center for balance signals, as key drivers of these responses. These neurons act through two separable outputs: a projection to the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray that promotes MS-like behavior, and a projection to the nucleus of the solitary tract that contributes to nausea-related aversion, likely through the parabrachial nucleus. Anticipatory tone cues recruit an inhibitory pathway from the central amygdala to suppress Cbln2+ MVN neurons. These findings reveal how auditory prediction can dampen vestibular circuits that drive MS.

papers.abstract: Nanofluidic ion gating underpins both biological signal transduction and iontronic signal processing. However, a simple and reliable mechanism that functions independently of local electrochemical conditions remains unavailable, hindering interference-free integration of artificial iontronic components with biological counterparts. Here, we present a nanofluidic device that enabled ionic gating through pervaporation-driven precipitation and rehydration-driven dissolution (PP&RD) of salt solutions within a nanochannel. Pervaporation induced local salt precipitation in the nanochannel, forming an electrical blockage that suppressed conductance (OFF state), whereas rehydration dissolved the precipitate and restored the conductance (ON state). The ionic gating device exhibited an ON-OFF conductance ratio exceeding 100, fully reversible operation performance, and robust switching across experimental conditions. By integrating two ionic gates in parallel or in series within a single device, we further implement Boolean OR and AND logic operations. PP&RD-based ionic gating thus provided a simple, versatile, and practical foundation for scalable iontronic circuit architecture.

papers.abstract: Uncovering general principles connecting neural circuits to behaviour requires comparative brain analyses across species. To advance these efforts, we developed a standardised workflow and a unified brain atlas platform for the quantitative comparison of neural structures between two teleost larvae, medaka (Oryzias latipes) and zebrafish (Danio rerio). Crucially, the platform seamlessly integrates user-generated image volumes, facilitating quantitative comparisons of anatomical, transcriptional, and functional data across species and laboratories. Utilising these integrated tools, we identified regional anatomical differences and differentially expressed genes between the species. We further demonstrated functionally distinct telencephalic regions in both species that exhibit divergent responses to social stimuli, suggesting an evolutionary divergence in social processing mechanisms. This web-based, interactive atlas platform promotes data exchange and knowledge sharing within the teleost community. Its scalable design permits effortless multi-group contributions, enabling expansion into a continuously growing, globally accessible database.

papers.abstract: Understanding charge carrier recombination kinetics is vital for optimizing perovskite materials and devices. Time-resolved photoluminescence (TrPL) is widely used to investigate carrier kinetics, but kinetic parameters inferred from TrPL alone often suffer from intrinsic non-uniqueness. Therefore, quantitatively resolving complex multichannel recombination processes remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the non-uniqueness problem in TrPL. Through incorporating TrPL with excitation-dependent photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), the non-uniqueness problem is substantially alleviated. Based on this insight, we develop a deep learning (DL) framework to extract kinetic parameters from joint TrPL-PLQY profiles. This framework avoids repeated iterative parameter optimization for each new dataset within the predefined kinetic model. The DL model is trained on a large dataset generated from physically grounded simulations. Six physically relevant key kinetic parameters spanning several orders of magnitude, namely, effective external band-to-band electron-hole bimolecular recombination coefficient (γeh), electron capture coefficient (γec), hole capture coefficient (γhc), trap density (NT), electron emission coefficient (γee), and Auger recombination coefficient (γAug), can be rapidly predicted. High accuracy is achieved, with coefficients of determination of 0.996, 0.938, 0.969, 0.988, 0.905, and 0.973 for the respective parameters. The framework is further validated experimentally. The DL-predicted kinetic parameters are physically consistent with device-level characterization results. Moreover, when working with PLQY, we identify a meaningful TrPL acquisition window (0-2 μs) and decay cutoff (at 0.01), providing guidance toward standardized TrPL characterization protocols. The proposed framework provides a fast and quantitative approach for disentangling complex recombination pathways. Further, this work represents a significant step toward data-driven analysis of perovskite semiconductor kinetics.

papers.abstract: Birds modulate wing-tail morphology to balance maneuvering capability and cruise efficiency, but fully replicating this mechanism in bio-inspired aerial robots increases actuator redundancy and control complexity. Here we present NPU-Sparrow, a micro flapping-wing robot that integrates a linkage-driven morphing tail with flapping wing incidence-angle control. Combining aerodynamic modeling, wind tunnel measurements and outdoor flight tests, we show that the negative-lift tail reconciles cruise stability with maneuvering performance through role reversal: it provides longitudinal static stability at low angles of attack, but becomes an auxiliary lifting surface above 13°. This low-degree-of-freedom strategy expands the level-flight speed envelope to 4.5-13.2 m s-1, achieves a peak roll rate of 375° s-1, reduces steady-turn radius by 20.4% and enables loops and barrel rolls. In this work, we show that translating avian wing-tail coordination into modelable engineering variables provides a route towards agile and efficient flapping-wing robots.

papers.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized. We conducted a post hoc analysis stratified by chemotherapy class of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled AVERT trial comparing apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) with placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy. The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (CRNMB)) per ISTH criteria. A subgroup analysis compared platinum-based with non-platinum chemotherapy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusted for age, sex, and study site. Treatment-by-platinum interaction terms were used to assess effect modification by platinum exposure. A total of 563 patients were included and categorized by one or more chemotherapy classes at randomization. Compared with placebo, apixaban appeared to reduce VTE in patients on platinum (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.57), taxane (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75), taxane-platinum (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.68), topoisomerase inhibitor (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53), and antimetabolite regimens (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.54), without increased bleeding. Among placebo-treated patients, platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with a higher risk of VTE compared with non-platinum regimens (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.48-3.42), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed among apixaban-treated patients. Treatment-by-platinum interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by platinum exposure. In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis, apixaban thromboprophylaxis was associated with reduced VTE across several chemotherapy regimens with generally acceptable safety outcomes. Patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy may derive greater absolute benefit from thromboprophylaxis in the setting of higher underlying thrombotic risk.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Cognitive problems are common after breast cancer, yet few randomized controlled trials have evaluated interventions to address them. This study tested whether a 12-month exercise intervention improved cognition in breast cancer survivors. Methods Breast cancer survivors (n = 253) were randomized to an exercise arm with a remotely delivered intervention or a Health & Wellness arm receiving calls on healthy aging topics at the same frequency. The 6-month intervention (primary end-point) was followed by a 6-month maintenance phase (secondary end-point). At baseline, 3, 6, and 12 months, participants wore an accelerometer and completed the PROMIS Cognitive Abilities Questionnaire, the NIH Toolbox Digit symbol test (Processing Speed), and a neurocognitive battery assessing memory, executive function, and attention. Linear mixed models compared outcomes between arms. Results The Exercise arm had greater increases in moderate to vigorous physical activity (18 minutes/day baseline, 23.5 minutes/day 12 months) than the Health & Wellness arm (15 minutes/day baseline, 15.5 minutes/day 12 months) at all follow-ups (P-values < .01). No significant between-group effects were observed for primary outcomes of self-reported cognition or processing speed at 6 or 12 months (P-values > .05). However, for secondary outcomes, the Exercise arm had greater improvements than the Health & Wellness arm in attention (6 months: b = 0.14, P = 0.03; 12 months: b = 0.21, P=.002), and memory (6 months: b = 0.18, P < .01). Conclusion A remotely delivered Exercise intervention was not superior to a Health & Wellness intervention for self-reported cognition or processing speed. However, secondary outcomes suggest sustained improvements in attention and short-term benefits in memory. Exercise warrants further investigation as a strategy to support cognitive health in breast cancer survivors. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04049695

papers.abstract: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is highly lethal owing to its early and aggressive metastasis, yet the underlying multi-layer molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood, limiting therapeutic advances. We performed integrative multi-omics profiling (including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and lactylome) on 99 matched primary tumor, metastatic lymph nodes, and normal esophagus tissue samples from 36 patients with metastatic ESCC. Molecular changes and cross-omics interactions associated with the metastatic cascades were characterized. Key findings were validated by immunohistochemistry and survival analysis in an independent cohort of 116 ESCC patients. Further functional and mechanistic studies were conducted using in vitro and a tail-vein experimental lung metastasis model. Our analysis revealed pronounced disturbance in immune-related pathways closely associated with metastatic progression and poor prognosis. Intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM1) was identified as a critical factor of ESCC invasion and metastasis. Additionally, lysine-lactylated proteins were predominantly involved in cytoskeleton, focal adhesion and glycolysis pathways during ESCC metastasis. Integrative analysis revealed that the lactylome interacts with the genome and transcriptome through both cis- and trans-regulatory mechanisms, primarily in immune and metabolic pathways. Notably, lactylation of phosphoglycerate mutase 1 (PGAM1) at residue K251 enhances its interaction with actin gamma 1 and promotes metastatic phenotypes. ICAM1 and PGAM1 K251 lactylation represent two independent metastasis-associated mechanisms identified from the same multi-omics dataset. This integrative multi-omics characterization provides a comprehensive resource for metastatic ESCC research and identifies K251-lactylated PGAM1 as a candidate prognostic biomarker and mechanistic lead warranting further preclinical validation.

papers.abstract: Dimensionality reduction and clustering are instrumental to single-cell and spatial genomics data analysis. Here we show that existing methods tend to fit oversampled classes and miss more unique signals and patterns, such as rare cell types and states. We find that the problem in such cases is not primarily data scarcity per se, but the model equating abundance with importance. Addressing this, we present "Distributionally Robust and latent Group-AwarE consensus Machine learning" or DR-GEM, a self-supervised meta-algorithm that uses the reconstruction error to reorient the model attention to patterns it initially missed and applies balanced consensus learning to increase robustness and filter low-quality data. We apply DR-GEM to synthetic and real-world single-cell, spatial transcriptomics, and Perturb-seq datasets and demonstrate that it outperforms existing methods in obtaining reliable embeddings, recovering rare cell types, filtering noise, mitigating cell-level and patient-level underrepresentation, and uncovering held-out genetic and spatial features. We thus surface and address an underappreciated problem and present a self-supervised framework to help support AI-based and data-driven discoveries.

papers.abstract: Abstract Occasional complete responses (CR) to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy demonstrate that acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) can be immunosensitive when appropriately targeted. In this study, we analyzed patients with AML/MDS (n = 14) who were treated with the anti-TIM3 sabatolimab and the hypomethylating agent decitabine in a phase Ib clinical trial (NCT03066648) using single-cell RNA and T-cell receptor (TCR) sequencing (n = 6) and functional coculture assays. Unlike T cell–restricted CTLA4 and PD1, TIM3 was broadly expressed across natural killer (NK) cell, myeloid cell, and T-cell populations. Therapy induced the expansion of cytotoxic NK cell subsets and enhanced type I IFN signaling. Fewer than 1% of bone marrow CD8+ T cells displayed a canonical exhaustion phenotype, and treatment preferably expanded small CD8+ T-cell clones in responders. Responders exhibited greater expansion of cytotoxic CD4+ T cells and B cells, as exemplified by a patient with preexisting CD4+ T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia (T-LGLL) achieving an outstanding CR lasting 23 months. More than 20% of this patient’s lymphocytes were T-LGLL cells expressing a TCR capable of recognizing autologous blasts. Overall, our results suggest that anti-TIM3 combined with decitabine engages a distinct mechanism of immune activation compared with anti–PD-1 and anti-CTLA4, preferentially expanding NK cell and CD4+ T-cell populations.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Cancer and its treatments are associated with accelerated biological aging and cognitive impairment among breast cancer survivors. DNA methylation-based epigenetic clocks provide measures of biological aging that predict morbidity and mortality, yet little is known about whether these aging trajectories can be modified by lifestyle intervention. This secondary analysis of a subset of participants in a randomized controlled trial examined the impact of a 12-month exercise intervention on markers of epigenetic aging among breast cancer survivors. Methods Sedentary breast cancer survivors within 5 years of diagnosis were randomized to a remotely delivered exercise intervention or a contact-matched health & wellness condition. Whole blood samples and cognitive assessments were obtained at baseline, 6, and 12 months. Epigenetic ages and differential methylation were calculated from normalized data obtained from the Methylation Screening Array. Results A subsample of 124 participants with complete data was analyzed. The Exercise arm showed slower epigenetic aging than the Health & Wellness arm over the 12-month study, according to GrimAge2 (P = .02) and DNAmFitAge (P = .002) clocks. Changes in epigenetic aging were significantly correlated with alterations in attention and self-reported cognition, with faster epigenetic aging associated with greater cognitive decline. Furthermore, genome-wide analysis of the blood epigenome identified differentially methylated sites, some mapping to genes enriched for BDNF (brain-derived neurotrophic factor) signaling pathways. Conclusion A 12-month exercise intervention was associated with slower epigenetic aging among breast cancer survivors. These findings suggest that biological aging may represent a modifiable mechanism through which exercise supports cognitive health in cancer survivorship. papers.abstract: The marked heterogeneity of primary liver cancer (PLC), together with the dynamic influence of the tumor microenvironment (TME), remains a major challenge to precision oncology. As currently available therapies provide limited benefit for many patients and robust preclinical platforms for rapid, patient-specific treatment stratification are lacking, there is an urgent need for models that faithfully preserve individual tumor architecture and cellular diversity. We established three-dimensional bioprinted primary liver cancer (3DP-PLC) models comprising 61 patient-derived monocultures and 34 co-culture models with patient-matched cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). To explore the correlation between ex vivo models and clinical drug response, we developed a clinically anchored hybrid stratification framework for response classification. In parallel, the 3DP-PLC/CAF co-culture biobank was used to investigate stromal regulation of therapeutic response. These 3DP-PLC constructs preserved the histological features, biomarker expression patterns, mutational landscapes, and transcriptomic profiles of their corresponding parental tumors. Drug-sensitivity profiling across the biobank revealed substantial intertumoral heterogeneity in therapeutic responses. The clinically anchored hybrid stratification framework integrating ex vivo pharmaceutical profiles with external clinical benchmark data enabled interpretable response classification and demonstrated clinical relevance in patients receiving neoadjuvant or adjuvant targeted therapy. In parallel, the 3DP-PLC/CAF co-culture biobank, combined with single-cell transcriptomic analysis, recapitulated fibrous ring-like architecture and revealed CAF-associated drug-resistant states. These findings support 3DP-PLC as a high-fidelity and scalable platform for personalized therapeutic stratification and mechanistic investigation of tumor-stroma interactions in PLC.

papers.abstract: The microglial extracellular traps(MiETs) were appeared in glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), but the underlying molecular mechanisms and functions were unknown. In this study, we aimed to explore the ability of GBM-derived UL16-binding protein 2 (ULBP2) on activating MiETs and manipulating microglia to support GBM development. Herein, ULBP2 was identified as a key upregulated protein in GBM and triggered MiETs formation. In turn, MiETs accelerated GBM malignant growth. Mechanistically, GBM released ULBP2 to connect with syndecan-1(SDC1) on microglia, the ULBP2/SDC1 complex induced lactylation of peptidylarginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) and following MiETs formation. Furthermore, MiETs stimulated GBM autophagy to promote proliferation and invasion. Our results demonstrated that GBM exerted a crucial role in MiETs formation through the ULBP2/SDC1/PAD4-Kla axis, and the interaction between GBM and microglia created a feed-forward mechanism for tumor progression. Thus, these data provided novel insights into a potential therapeutic target toward MiETs for preventing and suppressing GBM.

papers.abstract: Tumor progression and therapeutic failure are classically interpreted through the lenses of genetic evolution and ongoing signaling dynamics. However, increasing evidence suggests that tumors are also shaped by durable imprints of prior microenvironmental exposures. These prior exposures can leave persistent epigenetic and structural imprints that progressively stabilize adaptive cellular states, allowing transient responses to become durable regulatory programs. Chronic inflammation, metabolic stress, therapeutic pressure, and extracellular matrix remodeling induce persistent molecular states across cancer cells and stromal compartments, generating history-dependent phenotypes that influence future biological responses. Building on these observations, we propose that these adaptive processes collectively constitute a distributed tumor microenvironment (TME) memory encoded across cancer cells, fibroblasts, immune cells, endothelial cells, and the extracellular matrix (ECM), rather than representing isolated mechanisms of adaptation. We examine how TME memory contributes to therapy resistance, immune dysfunction, cancer-cell dormancy, minimal residual disease, and tumor recurrence, and discuss the molecular mechanisms underlying memory encoding, persistence, and recall. Finally, we discuss the experimental and clinical strategies required to identify memory-rich tumors, develop biomarkers of historical imprinting, and design memory-aware therapeutic interventions. By integrating diverse forms of adaptive persistence within a unified history-dependent framework, TME memory provides a conceptual foundation for investigating tumor evolution, therapeutic resistance, and future precision oncology strategies.

papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is clinically and biologically heterogeneous, and ethnic differences may influence its pathogenesis. However, single-nucleus transcriptomic data from East Asian populations remain limited. Here, we present a spatially resolved single-nucleus transcriptomic atlas of the human substantia nigra (SN) across the PD continuum, control, incidental Lewy body disease (iLBD), and advanced PD, in pathologically confirmed Korean individuals. Our integrative analysis revealed early α-synuclein aggregation in the ventrolateral SN, subtype-selective vulnerability of dopaminergic neurons, and relative preservation of the dorsomedial SN and ventral tegmental area. Trajectory and gene regulatory network analyses of astrocytes and microglia revealed spatiotemporally distinct, disease-associated glial responses, each driven by divergent molecular programs. We also identified two transcriptionally distinct vascular spatial clusters that exhibited differential vulnerability and remodeling. Spatial ligand-receptor analysis of α-synuclein-positive regions revealed intercellular signaling events associated with early pathology, including extracellular matrix remodeling and synaptic adhesion, which were prominent in the iLBD but largely diminished in advanced PD. Integration with PD genome-wide association studies using MAGMA demonstrated differential coupling between genetic risk, spatially resolved cell-state programs, and pseudotime-inferred microglial dynamics across ancestries. This study provides the first high-resolution, spatially mapped single-nucleus transcriptomic resource from an East Asian PD cohort, illuminating early perturbations in the midbrain intercellular and microenvironment that may underlie selective dopaminergic vulnerability and guide the development of ancestry-informed therapeutic strategies.

papers.abstract: The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor's spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4's groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

papers.abstract: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain. We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety. A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively. Among patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. papers.abstract: Whether endovascular therapy benefits patients with mild acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation is uncertain. We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized trial in China involving patients with acute ischemic stroke of mild clinical severity (defined by a score of <6 on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale) that had resulted from large-vessel occlusion involving the anterior circulation. Patients also had neuroimaging features of a small infarct core and a large perfusion-mismatch volume, representing substantial at-risk tissue, within 24 hours after symptom onset or after they were last known to be well. The patients were randomly assigned to undergo endovascular therapy and receive medical management or to receive medical management alone. The primary outcome was an excellent functional outcome (defined by a modified Rankin scale score of 0 [no symptoms] or 1 [no clinically significant disability]) at 90 days. A total of 304 patients underwent randomization, of whom 300 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population: 144 in the endovascular-therapy group and 156 in the medical-management group. At 90 days, a modified Rankin scale score of 0 or 1 was reported in 69.4% of the patients in the endovascular-therapy group and in 50.0% of those in the medical-management group (odds ratio, 2.32; 95% confidence interval, 1.41 to 3.81; P<0.001). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours occurred in 3 patients in each group. Serious procedure-related complications occurred in 19 patients (13.2%) in the endovascular-therapy group. Among all the participants, one death occurred (in the endovascular-therapy group). In this trial from China involving patients with mild acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion and substantial at-risk tissue on perfusion imaging, endovascular therapy performed within 24 hours after symptom onset plus medical management resulted in better 90-day functional outcomes than medical management alone, without an increase in the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage but with a high incidence of serious procedural complications. papers.abstract: Divarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib. In this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety. A total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; P<0.001). The median overall survival was 17.7 months with divarasib and 12.0 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for death, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.78; P<0.001). Of the 328 patients who could be evaluated for response, a confirmed response occurred in 58.4% in the divarasib group and in 32.3% in the control group. The median duration of response was 11.9 months with divarasib and 6.9 months with control treatment. Fewer grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were noted with divarasib (24.6%) than with control treatment (34.5%). Among patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. papers.abstract: The combination of docetaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab (THP) is an established first-line treatment for human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive advanced breast cancer. The efficacy and safety of anbenitamab, a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody, plus albumin-bound docetaxel (HB1801) in this context are unknown. In this phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted in China, we randomly assigned patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer in a 1:1 ratio to receive either anbenitamab plus HB1801 or THP. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Objective response was a secondary end point. A total of 885 patients were enrolled (445 were assigned to receive anbenitamab plus HB1801 and 440 to receive THP). At this prespecified interim analysis (with 401 events [disease progression or death] and a median follow-up of 21.0 months), the estimated 24-month progression-free survival was significantly higher with anbenitamab plus HB1801 than with THP (58.5% vs. 34.4%; hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.46; 95% confidence interval, 0.37 to 0.56; P<0.001). The percentage of patients with an objective response was 87.6% in the anbenitamab group and 73.4% in the THP group. Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 204 of 444 patients (45.9%) in the anbenitamab group and in 151 of 439 patients (34.4%) in the THP group. Neutropenia was the most common adverse event of grade 3 or higher in both groups (13.1% in the anbenitamab group and 8.4% in the THP group). Adverse events leading to death occurred in 2 patients in each group. Anbenitamab plus HB1801 led to significantly higher progression-free survival than THP among patients with HER2-positive advanced breast cancer. papers.abstract: The standard of care for patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer continues to evolve. Whether perioperative durvalumab, with or without tremelimumab, plus neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin is effective in such patients is unknown. In this phase 3 open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1:1 ratio, patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy to receive neoadjuvant durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin every 3 weeks for three cycles, followed by radical cystectomy and then adjuvant durvalumab every 4 weeks for nine cycles; neoadjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (tremelimumab for two cycles only), radical cystectomy, and adjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab (tremelimumab for one cycle only); or radical cystectomy alone (control). The dual primary end points were event-free survival in each of the two durvalumab groups as compared with that in the control group. The two durvalumab groups were not compared with each other. The key secondary end point was overall survival. In total, 233 patients were assigned to the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group, 233 to the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group, and 229 to the control group. Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 63.5% (95% confidence interval [CI], 56.5 to 69.7) with durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin and 45.1% (95% CI, 38.2 to 51.8) with control (hazard ratio for an event or death, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.38 to 0.67; P<0.001); estimated overall survival at 24 months was 78.4% and 69.4%, respectively (hazard ratio for death, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.40 to 0.83; P = 0.003). Estimated event-free survival at 24 months was 60.1% (95% CI, 53.2 to 66.2) with durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (hazard ratio for an event or death vs. control, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.47 to 0.80; P<0.001). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 71.1% of patients in the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group (treatment-related, 30.7%), in 79.5% of those in the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group (treatment-related, 44.5%), and in 50.2% of those in the control group. Perioperative durvalumab with or without tremelimumab plus three cycles of neoadjuvant enfortumab vedotin resulted in significantly better event-free survival outcomes than surgery alone. Perioperative durvalumab plus enfortumab vedotin led to significantly better overall survival outcomes than surgery alone. Grade 3 or higher adverse events of any cause were noted in more than half the patients in the durvalumab groups. papers.abstract: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy. In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety. Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group. Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

papers.abstract: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal. In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis. A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2. Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab.
